description:
Hello Team!

So I want some brilliant minds connecting together and exploring this beauty of space together.

Your challenge is to tell the story of some or all of this equipment that introduces school-age space enthusiasts to the hardware and the science it made possible.
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive 3D spatial storytelling engine developed using JavaScript with a custom Three.js and CesiumJS wrapper that transforms over 210,000 kg of discarded lunar and Martian hardware into digital monuments for young explorers. By integrating real coordinates, elevation maps, and telemetry from NASA datasets like LROC, NASA PDS, and Mars Trek GIS, the platform lets students orbit the Moon and Mars while listening to first-person rover audio diaries. This project directly addresses the challenge by reframing space debris—such as descent stages, heat shields, and rovers—into vital historical monuments rather than trash. It is critically important because it digitally preserves these artifacts against natural weathering like Martian dust storms and lunar micrometeorite abrasion, all while adhering to NASA's 2 km Keep-Out Buffer Policy and Article VIII of the Outer Space Treaty to protect historic sites from physical contamination.
details: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive 3D spatial storytelling engine that transforms over 210,000+ kg of discarded lunar and Martian hardware—such as descent stages, rovers, and heat shields—into digital historical monuments for young explorers aged 8–14. Built using JavaScript with a custom Three.js and CesiumJS WebGL wrapper, the platform integrates real orbital telemetry, elevation maps, and coordinates from the NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), LROC, and Mars Trek GIS. By combining 3D orbital views with first-person rover audio diaries and gamified badges, the project helps students explore historic landing sites while respecting NASA's 2 km Keep-Out Buffer Policy and Article VIII of the Outer Space Treaty. Ultimately, it preserves fragile interplanetary artifacts from Martian dust storms and lunar micrometeorite abrasion before they erode, inspiring the next generation by reframing "space trash" as monuments to human curiosity.
